 Dated this the 27th day of March 2015  J U D G M E N T Shaffique, J.

The writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking police protection inter alia contending that respondents 4 to 6, who were working in his establishment, which is a bakery, for some time has certain dispute in relation to employment.

The petitioner does not require to employ them presently and therefore, respondents 4 to 6 are obstructing functioning of the bakery as well as the borma situated in a separate building away from the bakery.
According to the petitioner, he is ready and willing to pay compensation to respondents 4 to 6 as fixed by the Labour Court or other competent authority.
A conciliation talk held by the District Labour Officer has failed because of the adamant stand taken by respondents 4 to 6.

It is submitted that now respondents 4 to 6 are making preparation for obstructing the functioning of the bakery by conducting agitation by blocking the entry to the bakery and also making preparations for attacking the petitioner, his workers, family members etc. 2 :-
2.

Learned State Attorney on instructions would submit that on receipt of the complaint from the petitioner, respondents 4 to 6 were called and they were asked not to create any physical obstruction to the functioning of the bakery and they should abide by the orders passed by the labour authorities.

3. Having regard to the aforesaid view of the matter, we do not think it necessary to issue notice to respondents 4 to 6.
4.

If there is any illegal obstruction being caused by respondents 4 to 6 in the matter relating to the petitioner conducting his business in his bakery/borma, the police shall ensure that no such obstruction is created by them.
With the above observation, this writ petition is closed.

Sd/-
ASHOK BHUSHAN CHIEF JUSTICE Sd/-
